links.comparator_used: Same five LLMs (GPT-4-turbo, GPT-3.5-turbo, Qwen2.5-14B, LLaMA3-8B, OpenBioLLM-8B) without RAG
links.outcome: Quality of answers to breast cancer guideline queries (rubric scores and pairwise ranking win rates), with human oncologist validation
links.effect: Absolute rubric gains 0.02-0.05 on a five-point scale; relative improvements in head-to-head win rates 16% to 46%; RAG-enhanced Qwen2.5-14B rubric 3.77 vs 3.96 for GPT-4-turbo and pairwise 0.72 vs 0.81
links.tradeoff: Absolute rubric gains were modest; human expert scores were more conservative than LLM judge scores (mean 3.81 vs 4.12); performance degraded sharply at higher context volumes
links.quote: Human expert scores confirmed RAG superiority but were consistently more conservative than LLM judge scores (mean 3.81 v 4.12 across all metrics).

links.comparator_used: Higher numbers of retrieved contexts (top-k values above 5)
links.outcome: Answer quality across different numbers of retrieved contexts
links.effect: Top-5 contexts was optimal; performance degraded sharply at higher context volumes (no numbers given in the abstract)
links.tradeoff: Performance degraded sharply when more contexts were supplied
links.quote: Optimal retrieval used top-5 contexts; performance degraded sharply at higher context volumes.

design_hint: retrieval grounding (RAG) added to existing LLMs
